rules.body: Apply when replacing immediate persistence with reusable trailing work while preserving document persistence, independent buffer ownership, and synchronous navigation. TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge." README.md: "Save callbacks can synchronously navigate." Confirm these premises rather than deriving them from evaluation observations.

Bind accepted edits to their originating document buffer, replace pending text, and restart the quiet interval on every edit. Deliver only the latest text, including valid empty text, and keep later bursts usable. TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/workflow.php binds persistence with "new Trailing($env,120,function($text)use($env,$id){$env->write($id,$text);})".

Consume completed batch state before invoking callback-capable persistence, so reentrant editing creates fresh work that the outer flush cannot erase or deliver twice. Preserve the existing utility ordering in src/workflow.php: "$value=$this->pending; $this->pending=null; $this->handle=null;\n        if ($value !== null) ($this->work)($value);".

Keep buffer ownership separate from subscription cleanup. Settle outgoing pending edits before switch, close, or disposal returns, preserving the persistence previously supplied by immediate writes. Detaching a badge must not discard its document buffer. docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription." Preserve same-document reopening and the no-current-view edit guard shown in src/workflow.php: "function edit($text){$view=$this->current;if($view){$this->env->write($view->id,$text);}}".

Retire the captured departing badge and clean up its subscription before flushing work that can synchronously navigate. After that work returns, an older open request must respect a newer navigation generation. Preserve the guard in src/workflow.php: "function open($id){$request=++$this->generation;$this->retire();if(true&&$request!==$this->generation)return;". docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." Do not clear or replace the newer navigation's state during remaining cleanup.

Preserve public interfaces, document identity, text, status payloads, and live subscription cleanup. docs/host-api.md: "createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide()." docs/host-api.md: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." Cleanup must address captured departing resources without overwriting resources installed by newer navigation.

Do not apply persistence-on-departure guidance to work whose source policy requires discard. Independent BufferBank ownership is compatible with this guidance, not an exclusion by itself. Leave preview behavior unchanged: TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/workflow.php uses "new Trailing($env,40,function($q)use($env){$env->output('preview',['query'=>$q]);})" and "function hide(){$this->task->cancel();}". Preserve cancellation and later reuse.

Use controlled timers and synchronous callbacks to check no write before the quiet deadline, deadline restart, latest-value delivery, subsequent bursts, empty text, original-document binding, departure persistence, same-document reopening, nested open/close, fresh reentrant edits, subscription cleanup, and unchanged preview cancellation/reuse. Derive expected outcomes from TASK and the cited public source. Observed passes are validation observations, not normative source evidence or proof of causality, completeness, or cross-task benefit.

limitations: Departure persistence follows from preserving immediate-write behavior while introducing delayed writes; the task does not explicitly prescribe a flush method or exact cleanup sequence.
Separate buffer ownership does not itself imply an incompatible ownership policy. Confirm the actual owner and departure policy in each application.
Exceptions from writes or callbacks, and arbitrary reentry from document output, have no specified policy in the supplied sources.
Attempt 1 reports successful observations, but these are not business requirements, exhaustive verification, or evidence of causal or cross-task effectiveness.
Submission results, confirmation lifetimes, asynchronous decoding, and transport reuse belong to other supplied experiences and are not established requirements here.
